I have farmed maize since I was a small girl watching my mother, and I know what this land needs. I will put manure from our goats and chickens on this plot because I own it and I want to keep the soil good, and if the agro-dealer has the subsidized fertilizer when I have a little cash, I will buy one bag for this field — that is what my neighbors do and I have seen it work. I do not trust those expensive new seeds; my own seed has never failed me completely, even when the rains are bad. My children and I will do all the work ourselves — clearing, planting, weeding twice, and harvesting — because I do not have money to pay workers, and we do not use chemicals since they cost too much and the maize does not need them if you weed properly. We wait for the rain here; there is no water for irrigation.
